Chip Industry Week In Review

16

Intel’s first 18A-P external customer; Siemens buys Breker; backside clock distribution; Microsoft taps EMIB; export controls tighten around China; Nvidia expands packaging capacity; SC26 brings new HPC HW; JEDEC previews DDR6; Europe pushes ahead with €33B in chip projects.

November 20th, 2026 -

By: The SE Staff

Deals and buys

Intel Foundry signed its first external customer for its advanced 18A-P semiconductor manufacturing process, according to Intel executives. The customer has not been identified, and Intel has not disclosed a production timetable.
Siemens plans to acquire Breker Verification Systems, a developer of AI-driven test suite synthesis and system-level verification technologies. The acquisition is expected to close in December.
Microsoft selected Intel Foundry‘s EMIB advanced packaging technology for custom silicon used in Azure’s infrastructure. The multiyear agreement also expands cooperation on Xeon processors, memory, and security technologies.
Infineon and Megmeet are teaming up on 800V DC power architectures for AI data centers, using Infineon’s gen-2 CoolSiC MOSFETs in three-phase power shelves.
GlobalFoundries and Boston Dynamics expanded their robotics collaboration to deploy autonomous Spot inspection robots across fabs in the U.S., Germany, and Singapore. GF also plans to begin evaluating Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid robots for semiconductor manufacturing tasks in early 2027.
AMD completed acquisitions of AI inference chip developer Taalas and AI model research company World Labs.

Funding

The European Commission said more than 20 semiconductor projects have been approved under the EU Chips Act, representing over €33B in public and private investment.
General Flash raised $128M to scale production of critical metals used in semiconductor and other industries.
Atom Computing finalized an up to $100M CHIPS Act R&D award for neutral-atom quantum computers.
Science Corporation raised $400M for its retinal implant chip that aims to restore form vision for certain types of macular degeneration.

Chip trade and export controls

The U.S. Department of Commerce introduced new restrictions addressing remote access to advanced U.S. AI computing through overseas data centers, along with new semiconductor licensing requirements affecting Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil.
The U.S. received license requests covering 3.4 million advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China and approved more than 879,000, according to U.S. government data. It is unclear how many were actually shipped.
TSMC and Samsung reportedly suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following new U.S. export restrictions, pending licensing approvals, per the Financial Times. TSMC is also reportedly halting affected Chinese customer orders at 16nm and below without U.S. approval and generally limiting those customers to 28nm and 40nm processes, provided those chips do not use HBM or advanced packaging.
The U.S. government released new details of an ongoing investigation into Megaspeed over suspected semiconductor export-control violations. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025, but its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix, later received more than $800M in Nvidia AI technology, mostly through third-party manufacturers, per the NYT. Nvidia says it blocked new orders and obtained government authorization for certain repair parts shipments. An investigation is underway.
The Trump administration is moving toward restrictions on Chinese optical transceiver imports, despite opposition from major U.S. cloud companies, reported Reuters.

Manufacturing capacity

Nvidia expanded its manufacturing agreements with Amkor, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL, TSMC, and others. The commitments cover additional substrate manufacturing, advanced packaging, and wafer capacity. As part of the expansion, ASE subsidiary SPIL signed a multibillion-dollar agreement with Nvidia to triple its advanced semiconductor packaging capacity in Taiwan by mid-2029, including new production lines for wafer bumping, assembly, and testing.
ASE Technology inaugurated the first phase and began construction of the second phase of its Lujhu advanced packaging facility in Kaohsiung, Taiwan.
Lam Research broke ground on a technology center in Zhunan, Taiwan, as part of its five-year, $3B global R&D expansion.
GlobalFoundries broke ground on a new 300mm semiconductor fab in Malta, New York, under a U.S.-Japan investment initiative providing up to $21B for two fabs. The first 300mm fab is expected to begin production in 2029.
ADEKA and Entegris agreed to collaborate on advanced semiconductor materials production in Japan.
Silicon Box advanced its proposed semiconductor packaging and test facility in Novara, Italy, into the basic design stage. The project is intended to establish additional European advanced packaging capacity for chiplet-based semiconductor devices.

SC26
The annual supercomputing conference kicked off this week in Chicago.

Nvidia announced a Rubin HPC GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores on a single GPU, along with sparse data acceleration capabilities. It also announced a 192-CPU Vera rack-scale platform for HPC with more than 200TB/s of aggregate peak memory bandwidth.
Penguin Solutions unveiled a photonics-based HBM-class memory appliance that uses Marvell technology to enable CPUs and GPUs to share memory across servers.
Lambda is deploying Nvidia’s CPO switches to connect GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs. Nvidia claims up to 5× better power efficiency and 15× higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics.
AMD announced that its Lux supercomputer at ORNL, powered by EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPUs, is now open to scientific users.

Fig. 1: Chicago’s SC26 event this week. Source: Liz Allan/Semiconductor Engineering
Reports and analysis

NAND flash contract prices are expected to decline in 2027 as Chinese cloud providers cut enterprise SSD orders amid GPU shortages and high inventories, reports TrendForce. Global NAND capital spending is projected to rise ~27% to ~US$30B.
CSIS examined the risks of using Chinese memory chips, including CXMT DRAM, citing security and supply-chain concerns. The report recommends restricting their use in sensitive government systems and expanding independent chip testing.
China still trails in leading-edge semiconductor fabrication, HBM, and chip manufacturing equipment, but it’s trying to work around those gaps through DUV multi-patterning, advanced packaging, 3D stacking, and photonics, said the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission in its annual report to Congress.

Standards

JEDEC previewed the DDR6 specification. While still subject to change, the current plan includes higher data rates and a wider bus, a pseudo-channel architecture, optimizations for die stacking and high-capacity modules, and data-center-focused low-power modes.
JEDEC also started a System Level Reliability Testing subcommittee to develop qualification methodologies, reliability practices, and evaluation approaches for emerging system applications.

Earnings and chip stocks

Year-over-year revenue change: Keysight Q4 up 40%; Kulicke & Soffa Q4 up 131%; Nvidia Q3 up 103%; and Soitec Q2 up 50% (at constant currency).
Notable: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said during the earnings call that the company has stopped shipping licensed Hopper AI chips to China, and its Q4 outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China. The company also established an oversight committee for national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risk management.
Check out the comprehensive chip stock chart for the latest impacts.

People

Cirrus Logic President/CEO John Forsyth was elected chair of the Semiconductor Industry Association, succeeding AMD CEO Lisa Su. GlobalFoundries Executive Chairman Tom Caulfield was elected vice chair.

Global
Americas

ACM Research opened a new research and manufacturing facility in Hillsboro, Oregon, as part of a U.S. expansion. The facility supports development and production activities associated with the company’s semiconductor wet-cleaning and electroplating equipment.

Europe

imec opened a photonics R&D center in Espoo, Finland, expanding its capabilities in optical design, simulation, testing, and system development.

Asia

imec established an R&D presence in Hokkaido, Japan, focused on photonic ICs, electronic-photonic integration, and CPO for AI and HPC.
SK hynix detailed plans for a jointly funded ₩874.6B (US$655M) semiconductor testing facility at its Yongin complex in South Korea. The cleanroom is scheduled to open in May 2027.

New Technologies
OpenAI reported advances in AI-assisted chip design, including RTL generation and design optimization for AMD processors and RISC-V cores. It is also working with Synopsys to train AI models to use EDA tools.
Advantest expanded its V93000 EXA Scale test platform with the new EXA Scale QX test head for high-power, high-pin-count AI and HPC devices. The four-card-cage architecture provides 36 instrument slots, increasing test capacity while maintaining compatibility with existing V93000 instruments, wafer probers, and test handlers. The system is expected to become available in Q1 FY2027.
Kulicke & Soffa shipped its first fluxless thermocompression bonding systems for panel-level packaging to two customers in Taiwan, supporting larger, higher-density packages for AI and HPC chips.
Siemens and Microsoft are planning to bring Simcenter X to Microsoft Azure, enabling engineering teams in automotive and other industries to run multi-domain simulations and scale HPC workloads in the cloud.
Keysight expanded its 6G sensing and communications testing capabilities with Cohere Technologies‘ Zak-OTFS technology to simulate multiple drones and their wireless communications under realistic radio conditions.
Infineon introduced a TMR-based magnetic switch, combining ultra-low current consumption with direct load switching in a single component. Applications include glucose monitoring, smart glasses, AR/VR devices, and medical disposables.
Microsoft made its Arm Neoverse CSS V3-based Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines generally available for cloud and AI workloads.
Vehicles

Rambus introduced security IP for 10 Mbps automotive Ethernet connections to edge nodes, built for 10BASE-T1S/T1L with low, predictable latency and up to 3× area savings.
Infineon‘s silicon carbide power module for drivetrain inverters is now available, extending its HybridPACK HD portfolio to heavy-duty applications such as long-haul transport, electric buses, and coaches.

Research
A KAIST team created a clock distribution network with a backside clock mesh in BSPDN architecture, with experiments demonstrating “26% lower maximum local clock latency, 40% smaller global skew, and 29% less mesh switching power on average than the frontside baseline.”
Nanjing University researchers developed CMOS circuits with 2D MoS₂ and 1D carbon nanotube transistors.
Researchers at UC Irvine and Samsung Electronics created topology-optimized liquid-cooling cold plates to reduce thermal crosstalk between AI processors and HBM.
Researchers at Tampere University and the University of Southampton developed wafer-scale ferroelectric transistors using MoS₂ and hafnium-zirconium oxide (HZO) for nonvolatile, multibit memory.
Uppsala University researchers proposed using co-packaged optics to broadcast LLM weights from centralized memory, reducing HBM requirements.

Security
SEALSQ signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Australia-based QuintessenceLabs, combining secure chips with quantum random number generation and enterprise key management.
Alerts and announcements

AMD disclosed a critical Platform Security Processor boot ROM vulnerability affecting Zen/Zen+ processors that can let attacker-controlled firmware bypass secure-boot authentication and execute unsigned code with full PSP privileges. AMD does not plan to release a mitigation because the vulnerable boot ROM cannot be modified.
Intel issued a security announcement on a DDR5 rowhammer attack that researchers used to bypass certain protections, induce bit flips on systems with 12th- and 13th-gen Core processors, and escalate privileges. Intel recommends keeping platform firmware, BIOS, and operating systems current.

Security Research

A University of Luxembourg team identified new security risks in Nvidia GPU load/store units. Two timing side channels enabled full AES-128 key recovery and covert communication between processes under Nvidia’s Multi-Process Service (MPS).
University of Kansas and Cornell researchers demonstrated a practical low-bandwidth memory denial-of-service attack that caused more than 1,000× slowdowns on DDR5- and HBM2E-based systems while consuming less than 1 GB/s of memory bandwidth.
TU Berlin researchers demonstrated a physical attack on firmware TPM protections that can reset failed-login counters and bypass PIN lockout protections used by Windows Hello and BitLocker.

Government security news

Global government cybersecurity agencies in several countries warned about a Java/OpenJDK flaw that can allow remote code execution on affected x86-64 systems. CISA urged immediate patching.
The UK opened applications for a £2.4M open-source semiconductor security program for secure-by-design hardware technologies.
CISA alerts are here.

Trending Video
Physics Vs. Data: Lam Research‘s David Fried talks about different approaches to speed up simulations, how to account for process variability with angstrom-level accuracy, and how to optimize systems for different memories and packaging options.

Quantum Hardware
Altera, OQC, and Nvidia demonstrated an FPGA-based quantum controller that uses an Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA to connect a superconducting QPU to Nvidia GPUs for real-time control and readout. The reference design reduces the need for external RF conversion hardware.
Quantum Machines demonstrated real-time quantum error-correction processing using its OPX1000 quantum controller and Nvidia CUDA-Q over NVQLink. Tests using simulated error data achieved 2.4 microseconds of round-trip latency with a CPU-based decoder. GPU-based decoding is planned.
IBM, Nvidia, and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory announced plans for a quantum-classical co-design platform, combining IBM quantum computers with Nvidia DGX B200 systems to research modular quantum architectures, scientific applications, and supercomputing integration.

Workforce, Education
A live 48-hour Student Cluster Competition was held at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago, where teams of six undergraduate students built and ran their own high-performance computing clusters. And the winner is TBD.

Fig. 2: Student Cluster Competition at SC26. Source: Brendan Heffernan/Semiconductor Engineering
University at Albany and Swagelok Albany launched a semiconductor workforce training partnership for lithography, advanced patterning, vacuum and plasma technologies, etch/deposition, metrology, and cleanroom operations.
University of Arizona, Pima County, and Taiwan’s NYCU opened a new semiconductor talent and innovation hub in Tucson for hands-on training, academic programs, exchanges, and networking with semiconductor employers.
